sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the test tools and the two anti-cheat functions, lockAllowed and anomalyFlags.
sections.why: Lets the rest of the file call these functions directly.

sections.name: t
sections.title: Fixed timestamp helper
sections.what: Turns a number of seconds into a fixed UTC timestamp on one fixed date, so the timing tests are exact.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes tests about order and gaps between calls repeatable.
sections.watch_out: The date and UTC handling are fixed here. Changing the timezone logic would move every timestamp.

sections.name: anti-cheat basics (anticheat)
sections.title: Lock and anomaly rules
sections.what: Checks that a live call locks only before the feed cutoff, that a historical moment never reveals before it is locked, and that an invalid time throws an error. Checks that burst locking, implausible streaks and always-maximum confidence are flagged, and that varied confidence is not flagged.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops cheating after the result is known and reports odd patterns for review without punishing ordinary fans automatically.
sections.watch_out: The flags are meant to be advisory. If any code blocks a user because of a flag, it goes against the design these tests describe.

summary: Checks the rule that stops a call from being locked after the ball has already been bowled, and the rules that flag unusual calling patterns without acting on them.
purpose: Keeps fans from locking predictions after the outcome is known, and gives reviewers warnings about suspicious patterns.
why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the comments, which mention decision D-040 for the historical reveal rule.
how: Builds timestamps from a helper, then checks the lock rule for live and historical modes and rejects a bad time value. Then runs the anomaly rules on generated call lists for burst locking, long streaks of hits, and always-maximum confidence.
inputs: Synthetic timestamps and call lists created in the test.
outputs: Pass or fail results from vitest.
risks: The flag thresholds are fixed by the test numbers. The tests assume UTC time, so a change in time handling would shift every timing result.
debug: If lock tests fail, compare the server time and feed cutoff values used in the failing line. If flag tests fail, check the counts and confidence values in the anticheat engine.
